back: Each training row uses only feature values that were known at that row's timestamp, never later values.

front: Which pandas function does a point-in-time join?
back: pd.merge_asof with direction='backward', sorted keys, by=entity and an optional tolerance.
Features are computed differently in training and in serving, so the model sees different data online than it saw in training.
Offline store: full feature history for training. Online store: latest value per entity for fast reads when serving.
It rejects stale feature values. You get NaN instead of using a value that is too old.

front: Why is a date-only join dangerous?
back: A value computed late in the day gets attached to earlier events of the same date. That is leakage.
